topic: P2-E build/verify friction log: local syspolicyd wedge, lane fallback details
notes: Opened per operator instruction to track lane friction. Context: P2-E successor session. HOST FRICTION (not lane): (1) rtk-wrapped cargo invocations backgrounded by the harness stop draining output and wedge cargo+rustc on the build-dir lock; three orphaned trees piled up serially on target/debug/.cargo-lock; swept via kill after lsof identified holders. (2) After lock cleanup, local rustc wedges loading FRESHLY BUILT proc-macro dylibs (e.g. libderive_more_impl dylib open at 16+ min, 0% CPU, heavy STIME) - the documented macOS syspolicyd/Gatekeeper assessment stall; `sample` on the wedged rustc also hangs. Local compiles unusable this cycle; possibly a pending TCC consent on the host (operator: check System Settings for a pending consent dialog). Fallback: claimed warm pool lane bpool3 (~/lanes/bpool3/blackbox @ 1955d5627a82); syncing branch beta/blackbox-v2 @ 6bec2d07 + uncommitted P2-E working set via patch; all checks/tests lane-side until the host unwedges. Lane friction details will be appended here as encountered.

Host toolchain RECOVERED: a fresh local cargo check -p bbox-corpus-core completed in 4m16s (exit 0) with no wedge; the syspolicyd assessment queue appears to have drained on its own (~90 min after first observed). No operator TCC action was taken as far as this session knows. macOS bootsmoke binary builds are feasible again. Lane bpool3 remains the gate path for all workspace-scale checks/tests (fast + reliable); local host reserved for the arm64 daemon/CLI smoke builds per the repo contract. Lane friction encountered so far: none beyond my own sync procedure error (git apply refused over a leftover untracked file; fixed by reset --hard + clean -fdq before each patch apply; lane is single-tenant to this session so the full reset is safe).

Kimi review friction: round 1 of the closing implementation review (session eacfe172-e883-4283-a9cb-340f46d74689) was terminated by the harness print-mode background-wait ceiling (600s) while its six background reviewer agents were still running - no verdict was issued; the reviewer had completed boundary verification and plan reading. Remedy per the harness's own message: CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0 on the claudew invocation. Resumed the SAME session via `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0 scripts/kimi-review.sh resume` (bookend discipline: no fresh session; the round produced no verdict so no scope was narrowed). If review rounds routinely exceed the ceiling, scripts/kimi-review.sh should probably export this env itself - flagging as a candidate repo fix after the bookend closes (not mid-review).

Closing the friction log with the arc: host syspolicyd wedge self-recovered mid-session (~90 min); lane bpool3 carried every workspace-scale gate flawlessly through 10+ sync/test cycles (the reset-hard + clean + apply-patch cycle was the reliable sync shape; my one apply failure was an ordering slip, not lane trouble) and is now released. OUTSTANDING TOOLING FOLLOW-UP for a future session (not committed post-PASS by bookend discipline): scripts/kimi-review.sh should export CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0 for its claudew invocations - both review rounds only completed because the orchestrator exported it manually; the default 600s print-mode ceiling kills any review whose reviewer fan-out runs long, and round 1 lost its first invocation to exactly that. Also worth noting for future heavy sessions: rtk-wrapped cargo, when a harness background timeout orphans it, stops draining output and wedges the build-dir lock chain; sweep orphaned cargo/rustc trees by lock-holder pid (lsof target/debug/.cargo-lock) before diagnosing deeper.

Friction log closed; the arc it tracked (P2-E + Phase 3 gates) is complete at exact PASS. Lessons absorbed into practice: orphaned rtk-wrapped cargo wedging the build-dir lock chain recurred in Phase 3 exactly as documented here (sweep by lock-holder pid remains the remedy; the Phase 3 fold hit it on bpool1); syspolicyd assessment stalls self-recover in ~90min; lane sync shape (reset --hard + clean -fdq + apply patch) held reliable through both phases. The one outstanding tooling follow-up (scripts/kimi-review.sh should export CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0 itself; both Phase 2 AND Phase 3 bookends only completed because the orchestrator exported it manually) is carried as a chore in the catalog-phase4 handoff thread.
